problem.name: Directed fixed-length path containment
problem.statement_latex: Fix a positive integer $k$. Given adjacency-matrix access to a directed $n$-vertex graph, decide whether it contains a simple directed path with $k$ edges. Complexity counts adjacency queries.
problem.statement_text: Fix a positive integer $k$. Given adjacency-matrix access to a directed $n$-vertex graph, decide whether it contains a simple directed path with $k$ edges. Complexity counts adjacency queries.

quantum.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(n^{3/2-\alpha_k})$ queries by Cornelissen--Gilani--Patro, where $\alpha_k=\Theta(c^{-k})$ and $c=\sqrt{3+\sqrt{17}}/2$, with the exact recurrence in their path-containment theorem.
quantum.headline_text: $\widetilde O(n^{3/2-\alpha_k})$ queries by Cornelissen–Gilani–Patro, where $\alpha_k=\Theta(c^{-k})$ and $c=\sqrt{3+\sqrt{17}}/2$, with the exact recurrence in their path-containment theorem.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n^2)$ worst-case adjacency queries for fixed nonempty paths; classical color coding or algebraic path detection follows input acquisition.
classical.headline_text: $\Theta(n^2)$ worst-case adjacency queries for fixed nonempty paths; classical color coding or algebraic path detection follows input acquisition.
